contents.name: Fixed-dimension best-rate question, Roth lower baseline, conjectural logarithmic exponent, and planar boundary, printed pp. 17–19
contents.support: The Status section records these statements as source-reported context. Roth's bound is explicitly only a classical baseline, not a claim that it is the strongest known lower bound.

contents.name: Theorem 15.7: Hammersley construction and its discrepancy order, printed p. 27
contents.support: This supplies upper-order context for the open formulation; it is not used as a proof of a matching lower bound.

sources.title: Josef Dick, Optimal Polynomial Tractability Exponents for the Inverse Star Discrepancy, version 3
sources.locator: Version dated 2026-10-15; §1, Theorems 1.1–1.2, and Remarks 1.3–1.5, especially Remark 1.4, PDF pp. 1–4.
sources.source_kind_detail: Author-uploaded 12-page arXiv v3 PDF; direct submission history identifies v3 as the version dated 2026-10-15.
sources.not_read: Only §§1–3 and the bibliography are reported read in the ROOT source packet; the paper's result is used only to delimit the fixed-dimension question, not as an accepted proof supplier.

contents.name: Theorem 1.1: lower bound in polynomially growing dimension strips
contents.reason: This result concerns a regime where dimension grows with inverse accuracy, whereas the open question fixes d before n tends to infinity; its strip bound is not used as a fixed-d lower result.

contents.name: Theorem 1.2: optimal uniform polynomial tractability exponents for inverse star discrepancy
contents.support: The Status section distinguishes this uniform growing-dimension conclusion from the fixed-d asymptotic order; no step of this paper is treated as a proof supplier.

contents.name: Remark 1.4: fixed-dimensional obstruction and construction upper bound
contents.support: This explicitly separates the growing-dimension tractability theorem from each fixed-d ray and does not provide a matching fixed-d lower bound.

contents.name: Remarks 1.3 and 1.5: polynomial-strip gap and comparison with the Hinrichs lower bound
contents.reason: These remarks compare joint d-and-accuracy regimes and inverse-discrepancy lower bounds; they do not identify the exact fixed-d logarithmic exponent asked for here.

read_evidence.access_method: The current web reader opened the full 12-page v3 PDF; the ROOT source packet records direct PDF retrieval and inspection of §§1–3, including the main results and Remarks 1.3–1.5.
read_evidence.extent: The title/version, fixed-d definition and distinction in Remark 1.4, and the relevant Theorem 1.1–1.2 statements were inspected. The source is used only for scope/status comparison; no preprint proof acceptance is asserted.
